statements.impact_statement: OpenSSH host key handling use-after-free. The restic image carries the ssh client binaries (openssh-client-common, openssh-client-default and openssh-keygen 10.3_p1-r0) in its Alpine layer. Nothing that runs the image starts ssh: restic runs it for an sftp: repository (observed), and all nine workloads (the database, OpenBao and etcd backup CronJobs, the two restore tests, the dump load test, the backup verifier and the two audit-sink shippers) build their repository URL with a fixed `s3:` prefix (in the script, or in the ExternalSecret template for the shippers); none of their scripts calls ssh, sftp, scp or ssh-keygen.
statements.action_statement: Re-check on restic 0.19.2 (0.19.1, built 2026-07-05, is still the newest tag on GitHub and Docker Hub on 2026-11-04; no fixed tag exists). Drop this statement once a fixed tag is pinned. Re-read at once if a script ever uses an sftp: or rclone: repository or runs ssh.
statements.status_notes: Expires: 2026-12-04. Renewed 2026-11-04 (first recorded 2026-10-22) after re-reading the bodies of the nine manifests and scripts that run the image (databases, openbao and etcd backup, both restore tests, dump-load-test with restic-dump.sh, backup-verify with restic-stage.sh, both audit-sink shippers with ship.sh) and a search of apps/, scripts/ and .github/ for ssh, sftp, scp and ssh-keygen (no call to any of them). Then run in the image against a fake S3 store with a failing stand-in for each ssh client first on PATH: 0 calls; the same image on an sftp: repository calls ssh at once. No cluster was used.

statements.impact_statement: Go crypto/tls session resumption in the kustomize binary bundled in the toolbox image. Our Jobs run kubectl, jq and curl, never kustomize.

statements.impact_statement: PyJWT 2.13.0 public key handling (fixed in 2.14.0). In the PostgreSQL images (16.15 and 18.6 carry the same PyJWT, msal, google-auth, botocore and certifi versions) PyJWT is a dependency of msal, which the Azure path of barman-cloud uses, and google-auth imports it for Google ID tokens. Neither is configured: every ObjectStore is S3, and the Clusters archive WAL through the Barman Cloud plugin sidecar, a separate image (plugin-barman-cloud-sidecar), not through the barman-cloud commands of the PostgreSQL image, which no manifest runs. The Python we run in the PostgreSQL image is dump_load.py and restore_cnpg.py (standard library only) and barman_check.py (boto3 on S3): run in the 18.6 image, it loaded no jwt, msal, azure or google module. No code we run there imports PyJWT, so the six HIGH PyJWT findings of 2.13.0 (below the CRITICAL gate) are not reachable either. This says nothing about certifi in the same images: botocore takes its CA bundle from certifi, so that finding is not waived.
statements.action_statement: Replace the image: no newer plain 18.x or 16.x tag exists on 2026-11-04 (18.7 and 16.16 are not published) and PyJWT 2.14.0 is the fix. Move to a newer PostgreSQL image (a new minor or the -standard-trixie variant, scanned first) in a dedicated exercise planned for 0.4.4, and drop this statement then. Re-read at once if an Azure or Google store, a barman-cloud command of this image or any use of PyJWT is introduced.

statements.impact_statement: certifi bundles emSign roots whose intermediate CA keys leaked (fixed in certifi 2026.10.19). It is a dependency of Python tools in the toolbox image; our Jobs run kubectl, jq and curl, which use the system CA store, and never start Python.

statements.impact_statement: certifi is only consulted by `requests`. In k8s-sidecar 2.14.1 `requests` calls only REQ_URL, and the Grafana chart sets it to http://localhost:3000 (plain HTTP, nothing to verify); the Kubernetes API client verifies against the ServiceAccount ca.crt (ssl_ca_cert), not certifi. Read in the image's sidecar.py, helpers.py and kubernetes/config/incluster_config.py, and in the rendered Grafana chart. Revisit if a sidecar URL annotation or an HTTPS REQ_URL is ever configured.

statements.impact_statement: Next.js 'use cache' functions returning typed arrays (next >= 16.0.0 and <= 16.4.0, App router with Cache Components). The feature is off in the Zitadel login build: cacheComponents, experimental.useCache and ppr are false in required-server-files.json, and the built chunks hold no RSC_SERVER_CACHE reference (read on the amd64 image of the v4.19.5 pin). These flags are the control. A search for the 'use cache' string is not a detector: the compiler consumes the directive, so the string is absent whether or not the app used it.
statements.action_statement: A fixed image exists since 2026-11-03: zitadel-login v4.20.1 ships Next.js 16.4.3. It is not bumped in 0.4.2 (no runtime change). Bump zitadel and zitadel-login together in the next release that changes the runtime, pinned as tag@index digest like the other pins (zitadel-login v4.20.1@sha256:1508e83275f1471b20ed42b159174e6b3e10e6c2481e64c0aee7ed5bfeeec18b; read the zitadel server tag and digest the same way), prove it on a cluster, and drop this statement then. The first drop condition, a tag with Next.js >= 16.4.1, is met by v4.20.1; the date that forces the bump is the expiry, 2026-12-04.

statements.impact_statement: Next.js image optimization endpoint (libvips memory bug in sharp on glibc, fixed in sharp >= 0.35.5; next >= 16.0.0 and <= 16.4.0). The login image is built on node:24-alpine (musl) and ships sharp 0.35.4 with glibc binaries only (@img/sharp-linux-x64 and its libvips, no linuxmusl package): require('sharp') from Next.js's directory fails there ('Could not load the sharp module using the linuxmusl-x64 runtime', run on the amd64 image of the pin; the arm64 image of the same index was not read) and Next.js 16 has no fallback, so the vulnerable code never loads. FRAGILE: it becomes reachable if the image is rebuilt on a glibc base. The Login V2 UI is routed through the Gateway since 0.4.0 (apps #161) and the optimizer path /ui/v2/login/_next/image is sent to the server, which answers 404, a rule that scripts/dev/test-zitadel-login-route.py keeps in place. The build also has dangerouslyAllowSVG false and no remotePattern; that is not the reason relied on here.

The first drop condition, a tag with Next.js >= 16.4.1, is met by v4.20.1; the date that forces the bump is the expiry, 2026-12-04. Re-check at once if the base image of the pinned tag changes.
